incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited shared hardcoded ASP.NET machine keys (CVE-2026-5426) across KnowledgeDeliver Learning Management System deployments to perform unauthenticated ViewState deserialization and gain remote code execution.
incidents.impact: Attackers planted an in-memory BLUEBEAM/Godzilla web shell, tampered with application JavaScript to push a fake security-plugin lure, and infected end users visiting the LMS with a Cobalt Strike BEACON backdoor uniquely keyed to the targeted organization.

incidents.victim: German university hospitals (Cologne, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Tübingen, Ulm, Mannheim)
incidents.vector: Unknown attackers breached Unimed, an external billing service provider used by multiple German university hospitals, in mid-April and exfiltrated patient records held on its systems.
incidents.impact: Roughly 95,000+ patients confirmed affected across six hospitals — Cologne (~30,000), Freiburg (~54,000), Heidelberg (~11,000) and others — exposing names, addresses, treating-physician details, and in hundreds of cases health and billing information. No clinical systems were disrupted; hospitals halted data flow to Unimed and are weighing legal action.

incidents.victim: European government organizations (Belgium, Italy, Serbia, Spain, Poland) and entities in South Africa
incidents.vector: China-aligned APT "Webworm" used open-source vulnerability scanners to find weaknesses in target environments, then deployed custom proxies (SoftEther VPN, ChainWorm, WormFrp) plus new EchoCreep and GraphWorm backdoors that abuse Discord and Microsoft Graph/OneDrive APIs for stealthy command-and-control.
incidents.impact: ESET found persistent espionage access at European government bodies, with stolen tooling and configurations staged in GitHub and a compromised AWS S3 bucket. The use of legitimate cloud services for C2 lets the activity blend with normal traffic and evade signature-based detection.

incidents.victim: Aerospace, defense and technology personnel in the U.S., Israel, UAE, and the Middle East
incidents.vector: Iran-nexus APT "Screening Serpens" sent tailored spear-phishing lures impersonating a global air carrier and a popular video-conferencing platform, delivering archives that used DLL sideloading and AppDomainManager hijacking to disable .NET security and load custom MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2 remote access trojans.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 attributed six new RAT variants deployed between February and April 2026 to attacks aligned with the regional conflict that began Feb. 28. Confirmed targeting in the U.S., Israel and the UAE, with operators rotating dedicated C2 domains per victim on Azure infrastructure for resilience.

incidents.vector: Method of intrusion has not been publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: NYC Health + Hospitals confirmed hackers stole medical data and biometric records — including fingerprints and palm prints — affecting at least 1.8 million people. The exposure of biometric identifiers, which cannot be replaced, makes the incident particularly serious.

incidents.vector: A criminal group known as TeamPCP compromised a GitHub employee's device via a malicious VS Code extension, then pivoted to internal source-code repositories.
incidents.impact: GitHub confirmed roughly 3,800 internal repositories were accessed; the group advertised the stolen code on a cybercrime forum, offered it for $50,000, and threatened to leak it for free. GitHub says no customer data was affected and that critical credentials have been rotated.

incidents.victim: Internet service providers, U.S. Department of Defense address ranges, and other DDoS victims
incidents.vector: The Kimwolf botnet enslaved Internet-of-Things devices typically firewalled from the wider Internet — such as digital photo frames and webcams — and rented or used the infected systems for record-breaking DDoS attacks.
incidents.impact: Ontario Provincial Police arrested a 23-year-old Ottawa man on a U.S. extradition warrant. Kimwolf was tied to DDoS attacks measured at nearly 30 Tbps, more than 25,000 attack commands, and victim losses exceeding $1 million in some cases. The takedown follows the March seizure of Kimwolf, Aisuru, JackSkid and Mossad infrastructure.

incidents.vector: A CISA contractor at Nightwing created a public GitHub repository ironically named "Private-CISA" and disabled GitHub's built-in secret-scanning push protection, exposing 844 MB of credentials, AWS GovCloud keys, SAML certificates, CI/CD logs and Kubernetes manifests since November 2025.
incidents.impact: GitGuardian's discovery prompted Congressional letters and demands for briefings. Researchers warned an attacker holding the keys could read source code across the CISA-IT GitHub organization, hijack CI/CD pipelines and modify deploy keys. CISA says there is no indication sensitive data was compromised but is still working to invalidate exposed keys.

incidents.victim: Stark Industries / WorkTitans / MIRhosting (Russian-linked hosting); Danish government bodies retroactively
incidents.attacker: Russia — state-linked influence and DDoS operators
incidents.vector: Dutch financial-crimes investigators (FIOD) raided three businesses and two data centers, seizing 800+ servers from WorkTitans BV and MIRhosting, which Krebs and de Volkskrant had previously identified as the remaining Internet conduit for the EU-sanctioned Stark Industries Solutions hosting network used by Russian intelligence services.
incidents.impact: Andrey Nesterenko (39) and Youssef Zinad (57) were arrested on May 18 and charged with violating EU sanctions. Reviewed traffic data showed WorkTitans and MIRhosting were the most-used networks in pro-Russian DDoS attacks against Danish government bodies during the November 2025 municipal elections. Customers of the.hosting were told their server data had been lost.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations in North America, Australia and the UK
incidents.vector: UNC6671 used high-volume voice phishing to impersonate internal IT, directing victims to subdomain-based lookalike SSO portals on enrollms[.]com, passkeyms[.]com and setupsso[.]com. Operators harvested credentials and MFA prompts in real time as an adversary-in-the-middle, then registered attacker-controlled MFA devices for persistence.
incidents.impact: Following access to Microsoft 365 and Okta environments, the group used Python and PowerShell against SharePoint, OneDrive, Salesforce and Zendesk to exfiltrate millions of files using captured session cookies. Extortion demands open in the millions, with escalation tactics including spam waves from Gmail accounts, threatening voicemails to executives, and swatting.

incidents.victim: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN customers (federal agencies and enterprises)
incidents.vector: UAT-8616 exploited a maximum-severity authentication bypass (CVE-2026-20182, CVSS 10) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager that lets an attacker present as a trusted network router and obtain administrative privileges with no credentials. Talos says infrastructure used by UAT-8616 overlaps with operational relay box networks. Separately, at least ten clusters chained earlier February-disclosed bugs (CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122) to deploy XenShell, Godzilla, Behinder web shells, Sliver, AdaptixC2 and XMRig miners.
incidents.impact: CISA added CVE-2026-20182 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and ordered all federal civilian agencies to patch by Sunday May 17 and follow earlier emergency directive hunt requirements. A single compromised controller can reroute traffic, intercept communications and push malicious configuration across every branch and cloud edge.

incidents.vector: Nitrogen, a ransomware group whose tooling is built from leaked Conti and ALPHV source, hit Foxconn's North American factories. The intrusion disrupted networks at Foxconn's Wisconsin facility, where employees reported Wi-Fi outages on Friday and were sent home before reverting to paper workflows.
incidents.impact: Nitrogen claims to have stolen 8 terabytes of data spanning more than 11 million files, including alleged confidential drawings tied to Intel, Apple, Google, Dell and Nvidia projects. Foxconn confirmed the attack and said affected factories are resuming normal production; ransom demand and full scope have not been disclosed.

incidents.victim: Instructure / Canvas (educational technology, ~9,000 schools and universities)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters breached the Canvas learning platform twice in two weeks — initially stealing data on May 1 and defacing the platform with a ransom message on May 7 — exploiting incident-response and vulnerability gaps that Instructure failed to fully close between intrusions.
incidents.impact: Instructure paid the ransom and says it received digital confirmation that the stolen data — names, email addresses, student IDs and student-professor messages from ~9,000 customers — has been destroyed. The shutdown disrupted millions of students during final exams; the House Homeland Security Committee opened an investigation into the company's incident response and disclosure practices.

incidents.victim: npm and PyPI ecosystem (TanStack, Mistral AI, UiPath, OpenSearch, Intercom, and ~169 packages)
incidents.vector: TeamPCP chained three GitHub Actions weaknesses against TanStack/router with no stolen credentials: a pwn-request fork executing in the base repo's runner context, GitHub Actions cache poisoning of pnpm artifacts, and OpenID Connect token extraction from runner memory to mint signed npm publishes. Within six minutes the worm pushed 84 malicious artifacts across 42 @tanstack/* packages.
incidents.impact: By end of day the campaign spread to 373 malicious versions across 169 npm packages plus PyPI packages, including @opensearch-project/opensearch, 57 @uipath/* packages, @mistralai/mistralai, intercom-client, and aviation-data packages. Roughly 520 million cumulative weekly downloads were in the affected window. The wave produced the first malicious npm packages carrying valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance, undermining a key supply-chain trust signal; the worm's source code was released publicly on May 12, accelerating copycat activity.
